en.title: Converting text to a number
en.story: A desk slip contains the text 12, but the next operation needs a number. Predict the result after the supplied conversion and addition. Quoted digits begin as a string. The conversion creates a numeric value from that text, and the final expression adds one numerically. This differs from deleting quote marks in source: input arrives while the program is running, so the program needs an operation that interprets the received text. Start with the valid digit-only examples here before exploring invalid input in later error-handling lessons.
en.idea: Conversion changes a value's representation for a new purpose. Java uses Integer.parseInt here, Python uses int, and JavaScript or TypeScript uses Number. The example stores the converted result under count while keeping the original text under digits. Converting does not secretly rewrite the original string. The supplied + 1 expression then produces 13 from numeric 12. In the independent exercise, the input contains only decimal digits representing a value from zero through 9999. Leading zeros are allowed, and printing the numeric value removes those unnecessary leading zeros.
en.make: Change the source text from 12 to 30, preserving its quotes and the conversion operation. Predict why the output becomes 31 rather than the joined text 301. The worked exercise labels the original text, converted number and resulting output. The independent program instead reads a digit-only line and prints the converted value without adding one. Keep that task's output rule separate from the lesson example. Compare the input 007 with expected output 7 to see why simply echoing the original line is not enough.
en.recap: Digits stored as text and a numeric value are different representations. Use a suitable conversion when a runtime string must participate in numeric work. Here the original string stays under digits and the new numeric value is stored under count. Valid-input rules matter: these examples do not claim that every arbitrary string converts successfully or identically across languages. Recall the role of each name before revealing the cards. The next module studies arithmetic and other operators more systematically, building on this distinction between values and their types.
